question: Should OpenClaw adopt `dummy/dummy` as a permanent credential-free core model contract, or keep deterministic message claiming plugin-owned while separately designing a real no-harness profile?
rationale: The patch works as demonstrated, but repository direction, existing hook contracts, persisted configuration semantics, and the claimed security boundary leave a product decision that cannot be safely resolved through a mechanical repair.

options.title: Keep It Plugin-Owned
options.body: Close or replace the core sentinel with a plugin using the existing message-claiming hooks, while retaining the linked issue for a genuine no-harness design.

options.title: Sponsor A Core Contract
options.body: Explicitly accept a core credential-free mode, then redesign the patch with truthful naming, complete config/auth/status semantics, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Accept A Convenience Sentinel
options.body: Treat the value only as a model-turn bypass, clearly disclaim any no-harness security guarantee, and own the long-term provider and compatibility exception.

recommendation.title: Keep It Plugin-Owned
recommendation.body: Close or replace the core sentinel with a plugin using the existing message-claiming hooks, while retaining the linked issue for a genuine no-harness design.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent model/provider and picker history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether the sentinel belongs in the permanent core contract.
